text.arabic_uthmani: كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُۥ مَن تَوَلَّاهُ فَأَنَّهُۥ يُضِلُّهُۥ وَيَهْدِيهِ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ

words.gloss_range: passive perfect decree or prescription, already written over the referent and governing a whole conditional proposition
words.root_gloss_range: writing, joining, registering, and binding decree; the local passive-plus-upon frame selects inscribed prescription while retaining durability and binding pressure
words.prose: {{ar:كُتِبَ}} ({{tr:kutiba}}) opens with a completed passive decree before the condition unfolds. The wording foregrounds the written verdict and leaves the decreeing agent outside the clause, so the whole following condition-and-consequence reads as already inscribed. The root keeps both record and binding pressure: this is not just a report but a legal sentence fastened onto its referent. It also shifts from disputing without knowledge (22:3) into record language that later surfaces in the surah's book-and-record field (22:8; 22:70).

topics.headline: settled passive decree
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins from a completed verdict, with the writer left unspoken and the decree itself foregrounded.
topics.reason: The QAC row identifies a passive perfect Form I verb, and attachment evidence leaves the agent unexpressed while the clause presents the decree as already standing.

topics.headline: whole proposition as written content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what is written is the whole conditional law, not a single bare punishment term.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following clause the complement of the passive verb, so the decree contains the condition and its consequence.

topics.headline: inscription with binding pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the decree as both written record and binding attachment, while the local construction keeps decree or prescription as the selected sense.
topics.reason: V4 supports writing, joining, and binding-decree branches; the local passive with an upon-complement selects prescription rather than making every branch independently active.

topics.headline: record thread across the passage
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a shift from disputing without knowledge into a written record field that will recur in the surah.
topics.reason: The critical rows name same-surah record links such as 22:70 and a boundary shift from 22:3; contextual profiles permit the root as an early record-thread marker.

words.gloss_range: upon, against, or concerning him; a bound prepositional pronoun that targets the preceding devil as the one over whom the decree rests
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}) anchors the decree before the content is disclosed. Its suffix reaches back across the ayah boundary to the devil described in 22:3, while the preposition gives the decree weight as something resting upon, concerning, and against that referent. The compact form binds burden and bearer before the conditional class opens.

topics.headline: boundary-crossing antecedent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah depends grammatically on the devil introduced in 22:3, so the decree is not free-floating.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence resolves the suffix to the preceding devil, making the boundary part of the local reference chain.

topics.headline: decree bearing down on him
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the decree as imposed on and adverse to its referent, not merely located near him.
topics.reason: The preposition is governed as the complement of the passive decree verb, and its suffix makes the burden-bearing relation definite.

topics.headline: target before content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the target of the decree is fixed before the sentence reveals the decree's content.
topics.reason: The local order places the prepositional dependent directly after the passive verb and before the content clause.

words.gloss_range: asserting and subordinating particle-plus-pronoun that turns the following condition into the decreed content
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:annahū}}) folds the following proposition into the decree rather than letting it stand as a separate assertion. The attached pronoun can be read as referential or as a matter-pronoun, but either way the particle turns the long condition and answer into one written content unit. Its first occurrence also prepares the doubled assertion frame that returns in the consequence.

topics.headline: embedded decree content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the condition is grammatically inside what has been written, not appended after it.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the particle introduce the content complement of the passive decree.

topics.headline: referential or matter-pronoun pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a pressure point between direct reference to the devil and a broader state-of-affairs opening, while local syntax keeps both within the same content clause.
topics.reason: The suffix is the governed noun of the particle; the ambiguity is useful, but it does not displace the content-complement function.

topics.headline: outer assertion frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the first assertion frame opening a nested legal structure that will be reinforced by the second occurrence.
topics.reason: The first particle opens the outer frame that contains the conditional protasis and apodosis.

words.gloss_range: open relative-conditional pronoun that defines a general actor slot by the act of taking the devil as patron
words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) opens the decree to an unnamed class. It identifies the person only through the act that follows, while the conditional force turns that conduct into a general rule. The decree therefore does not name a private case; it creates an open slot for whoever enters the patronage relation.

topics.headline: open actor slot inside the decree
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the decree is generalized through an open actor slot, not confined to a named individual.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the word as subject of the following verb and translation support marks the clause as conditional.

words.gloss_range: completed act of taking him as patron or ally; the attached object points to the preceding devil, and the local frame selects allegiance rather than turning away
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, succession, authority, alliance, patronage, and turning; the local Form V with direct object selects chosen patronage and governance-transfer, not withdrawal with a turn-away preposition
words.prose: {{ar:تَوَلَّاهُ}} ({{tr:tawallāhu}}) is the threshold act inside the condition. The attached object makes the allegiance personal and direct: the actor takes the preceding devil as patron, not merely an idea as influence. The root's nearness and patronage field makes following from 22:3 tighten into chosen jurisdiction, while the perfect aspect treats that alignment as completed before the ongoing consequences begin. Because this is direct-object patronage rather than the withdrawal construction, the root's turning range is narrowed toward active self-entry into patronage.

topics.headline: direct object of allegiance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that allegiance closes onto a specific patron through an attached object, with the local evidence resolving that object to the devil from 22:3.
topics.reason: A critical row notes possible role pressure, but attachment evidence resolves the object suffix to the preceding devil and makes the conditional person the subject.

topics.headline: completed threshold before consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that patronage is the completed threshold that releases the later imperfect misguiding and guiding verbs.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect in the protasis, while the consequence verbs are imperfect in the apodosis.

topics.headline: chosen patronage, not turning away
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the root's turning range narrowed to active self-entry into patronage because this local form lacks the withdrawal construction.
topics.reason: V4 supports both patronage and turning branches, but the direct object in this local frame selects attachment and alliance rather than withdrawal.

topics.headline: following escalates into jurisdiction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that following from 22:3 escalates into a governance-transfer relation whose consequences are then spelled out.
topics.reason: The root profile and critical rows tie patronage to later false and true patronage contrasts in the surah, while the local apodosis states this patron's governance.

words.gloss_range: consequential apodosis marker linking the condition to its asserted result with sequence and causation
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the hinge where the open condition becomes consequence. It marks the answer to the whoever-clause and attaches the result immediately to the act of patronage. The particle keeps the legal architecture from collapsing into loose description: first the condition is met, then the written result follows.

topics.headline: condition-to-consequence hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that misguidance is structured as the answer to the condition, not as an afterthought.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the preceding clause as protasis and the following clause as apodosis, with this particle marking the transition.

words.gloss_range: second asserting particle-plus-pronoun after the consequence marker, governing the two-verb apodosis and keeping the agent recoverable
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:annahū}}) reopens assertion inside the consequence. After the hinge, it makes the result emphatic and keeps the agent recoverable without repeating the noun. Because this second occurrence governs both later verbs, the apodosis becomes one asserted two-action outcome rather than two disconnected clauses.

topics.headline: asserted two-verb consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the consequence itself is asserted and stabilized inside the written decree.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence places the second assertion particle at the start of the consequence and coordinates the two following verbs under that frame.

topics.headline: agent carried by pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the devil as the agent of the following verbs even though the noun is not repeated.
topics.reason: The particle-pronoun form carries the subject continuity into the verbal predicate without an explicit repeated noun.

topics.headline: doubled assertion bracket
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the condition bracketed by two assertion frames, making the legal structure more than ordinary narration.
topics.reason: The repeated particle-pronoun form frames the outer content and then the consequence inside it.

words.gloss_range: ongoing causative misguiding of the conditional follower, with the object suffix routing the harm back onto that follower
words.root_gloss_range: straying from guidance, error, being lost, hidden, or made to disappear; the local Form IV selects causing another to stray while path-loss imagery remains active
words.prose: {{ar:يُضِلُّهُۥ}} ({{tr:yuḍilluhū}}) gives the first consequence of patronage as ongoing causative misguidance. The form makes the devil produce straying in the follower, not merely declare him astray, and the suffix carries that same follower inside the harmful verb. The root's lost-path and disappearance pressure makes the consequence feel like being driven out of recoverable orientation. This verb also opens a local misguidance-to-punishment thread that is taken up again nearby (22:9; 22:12).

topics.headline: causing another to stray
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the devil actively causes the follower to stray rather than merely exemplifying or naming error.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the local verb as Form IV, and the object suffix gives it transitive causative force.

topics.headline: ongoing harm routed to the follower
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same conditional person as the object of the ongoing consequence after his completed patronage act.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence resolves the object suffix to the conditional person, and the imperfect aspect contrasts with the completed condition verb.

topics.headline: path-loss and disappearance pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels misguidance as moral error and lost orientation, while local Form IV keeps the selected sense as causing the follower to stray.
topics.reason: V4 supports straying and hiddenness branches; the local causative verb selects producing straying, with disappearance retained as image-pressure.

topics.headline: misguidance-to-punishment thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this verb starts a local surah pattern where misguidance moves toward punishment, including the nearby reprise at 22:9.
topics.reason: The critical rows give concrete same-surah parallels at 22:9 and 22:12, and contextual profiles support the root's recurring misguidance field.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction that keeps misguiding and guiding as parallel actions by the same agent while adding the second consequence

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: causative misguiding of the same follower
guiding or conducting the same follower toward the punitive endpoint

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) binds {{ar:يُضِلُّهُۥ}} ({{tr:yuḍilluhū}}) and {{ar:يَهْدِيهِ}} ({{tr:yahdīhi}}) inside one consequence chain. The coordination keeps the same subject and the same affected follower in view, so the positive-sounding second verb does not cancel the first. It makes the irony visible as an ordered pair: path-loss, then a route to the endpoint.

topics.headline: coordinated antonym chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that misguiding and guiding are grammatically paired under one agent, creating the paradox that the endpoint must resolve.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the second verb as coordinated with the first under the same apodosis, not as a new independent clause.

words.gloss_range: guides or conducts him, but locally endpoint-governed toward punishment rather than beneficial guidance
words.root_gloss_range: guidance, leading, showing a way, direction, gifts, and offerings led to a destination; the local verb remains guidance-language while its endpoint turns it into false routing

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: directional preposition marking the endpoint of the guidance verb
the punishment of the Blaze as the endpoint phrase

words.prose: {{ar:يَهْدِيهِ}} ({{tr:yahdīhi}}) keeps the positive surface of guidance but makes it depend on {{ar:إِلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ilā}}) and the endpoint {{ar:عَذَابِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābi al-saʿīr}}). The same follower remains inside the verb through the suffix, so the one misled is also conducted by another toward punishment rather than self-orienting. The root's offering-led-to-destination branch darkens the route, while local grammar keeps guidance or conducting as the selected sense. That makes this satanic guidance the dark member of a same-surah contrast with divine guidance (22:16).

topics.headline: guidance turned by its endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb remains guidance-language until the endpoint reveals it as false routing to punishment.
topics.reason: The prepositional complement is syntactically forced as the destination of the guidance verb, so the endpoint governs the local force.

topics.headline: same follower under opposite verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same conditional follower through misguidance and guidance, making the irony grammatical as well as semantic.
topics.reason: The object suffix resumes the conditional person in parallel with the previous verb.

topics.headline: external guide rather than self-guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the follower is being conducted by another agent, not self-orienting, while the form keeps ordinary guidance-language in view.
topics.reason: The local verb is transitive with an object suffix and destination complement; related self-guidance forms remain contrastive rather than locally selected.

topics.headline: offering-led-to-endpoint image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the guided person as being led toward a destination like an offering, while local grammar keeps the surface verb as conducting toward punishment.
topics.reason: V4 supports offering and gift branches in the root family, but the local construction selects the guidance-to-endpoint reading.

topics.headline: dark member of a guidance axis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this satanic guidance to punishment contrasts with divine guidance in the same surah at 22:16.
topics.reason: Critical rows give the concrete 22:16 contrast, and contextual profiles support the root as a recurring guidance axis.

words.gloss_range: directional and terminal preposition that completes the guidance verb with punishment as its destination

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: guides or conducts him toward an endpoint

words.prose: {{ar:إِلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ilā}}) is where the positive surface of {{ar:يَهْدِيهِ}} ({{tr:yahdīhi}}) turns toward {{ar:عَذَابِ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābi}}). It governs the endpoint and prevents an absolute beneficial-guidance reading. The preposition carries both movement toward and arrival at a terminus, so the route and its punitive closure are grammatically joined.

topics.headline: destination hinge for false guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the irony of guidance becomes unavoidable at the preposition that supplies punishment as destination.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following punishment noun the governed destination complement of the guidance verb.

words.gloss_range: punishment or torment as the genitive endpoint of the guidance route, specified by the following Blaze construct
words.root_gloss_range: torment and punishment alongside fresh sweetness, withholding, and sensory branches; the local construct with the Blaze selects punitive torment while the sweetness contrast sharpens the absence of refreshment
words.prose: {{ar:عَذَابِ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābi}}) is governed by {{ar:إِلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ilā}}), so punishment becomes the endpoint of the false guidance route. As the first term of a construct with {{ar:ٱلسَّعِيرِ}} ({{tr:al-saʿīr}}), it receives specificity from the Blaze rather than standing as an abstract threat alone. The root's sweetness and refreshment branch is not the local sense, but it sharpens the fire endpoint by contrast: what arrives is torment without refreshment. The pairing also reads as a recognizable punishment-and-Blaze formula and places this endpoint in the local punishment thread that reappears near 22:9.

topics.headline: punishment as route endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that punishment functions like the destination reached by false guidance, not as a separate new event.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive under the preceding preposition and is attached as the destination complement of the guidance verb.

topics.headline: punishment specified by the Blaze
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the punishment defined through its fiery genitive, with specificity supplied by dependency rather than by an article on the head noun.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the following Blaze noun as the genitive complement, making the construct relation syntactically forced.

topics.headline: sweetness branch sharpened into torment contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses the punishment as a denial of refreshment at a fire endpoint, while local grammar keeps torment as the selected meaning.
topics.reason: V4 supports distinct sweet-water and torment branches; the construct with the Blaze selects torment and preserves sweetness only as contrastive pressure.

topics.headline: recognizable punishment-and-Blaze formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase belongs to a recognizable eschatological punishment register and opens a nearby punishment thread in the surah.
topics.reason: Critical rows and contextual collocation evidence identify punishment with the Blaze as a constrained phrase, with nearby same-surah punishment recurrence.

words.gloss_range: the definite Blaze as the genitive specification and final endpoint of the punishment phrase
words.root_gloss_range: kindling, stoking, blazing heat, burning agitation, madness, and other extended branches; the local noun selects the definite eschatological Blaze as sustained combustion
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسَّعِيرِ}} ({{tr:al-saʿīr}}) closes the ayah as a definite named Blaze, not a generic fire image. As the genitive complement of {{ar:عَذَابِ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābi}}), it specifies the punishment and supplies the final terminus of the whole chain: decree, patronage, misguidance, false guidance, punishment, Blaze. The root's stoking and sustained combustion pressure keeps the endpoint active, while its agitation and madness branch lets the fire mirror inner disorder after misguidance. The final sound texture lets the closure linger.

topics.headline: definite Blaze as final endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final destination is a known, definite Blaze that completes the entire consequence chain.
topics.reason: The noun is definite, singular, and genitive as the second term of the punishment construct, and it occupies the final word position.

topics.headline: sustained kindled fire
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the endpoint as maintained combustion, not a static place loosely called fire.
topics.reason: V4 supports kindling and blazing branches, and the local noun selects the Blaze with intensive active or passive fire force.

topics.headline: heat and disorder pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can sense misguidance terminating in both cognitive disorder and outer heat, while local grammar keeps the word as the Blaze.
topics.reason: The root has accepted burning-agitation and madness branches, but the local definite noun selects the fire endpoint and keeps those branches as image-pressure.

topics.headline: marked Blaze lexeme
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah closes on a marked Blaze term rather than a generic fire word.
topics.reason: The occurrence and collocation evidence support the word as a specific eschatological fire register.

topics.headline: semantic and acoustic closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final fire-name as closure in sound as well as meaning.
topics.reason: The final word position, definite surface, assimilation, and prolonged final sound all reinforce the endpoint function.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The passive KTB form, the WLY allegiance construction, and the coordinated DLL/HDY verbs with a stated destination form one causal sentence.
baseline_models.mechanism: A binding relational rule attaches to Satan: whoever allies with him grants him patronal leverage, is taken off right aim, and is then deliberately conducted to painful fire. DLL and HDY are sequential rather than contradictory because loss names departure from the right aim while guidance names directed conveyance to the wrong destination.

activation_trace.role: The decree branch makes the consequence binding rather than accidental.
Alliance and loyalty supply the relation through which the conductor gains leverage.
Departure from right aim supplies the first stage of the route.
Direction, course, and intended bearing supply the organized second stage.
Punitive pain identifies the route's harmful terminal condition.
Ignited fire gives the terminal condition a concrete destination.

changed_reading.before: A person follows Satan, is deceived, and is later punished.
changed_reading.after: Choosing Satanic allegiance activates a decreed routing relation: he first removes the follower from right aim and then purposefully conducts that follower to burning punishment.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The WLY form precedes two coordinated causative actions on the same pronominal object.
baseline_models.mechanism: WLY contributes adjacency and uninterrupted succession: attachment closes the interval between patron and follower. DLL then marks the follower as lost from the prior hold, while HDY pictures a leader going in front. The verse can therefore describe a two-stage handoff from dislocation to escorted arrival.

activation_trace.role: Nearness without an interval makes influence an attached relation.
Unbroken succession organizes the two following verbs as stages.
Loss from one's holder supplies dislocation before transport.
The leader or foremost element supplies an escort moving ahead of the displaced follower.

changed_reading.before: Misleading and guiding are an ironic pair of near-synonyms.
changed_reading.after: The pair is operational: attachment first makes the person lost from a prior hold and then hands that displaced person to a leader who goes ahead toward a fixed end.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The passive KTB predicate is imposed upon Satan and its content is a rule quantified over whoever forms WLY affiliation with him.
baseline_models.mechanism: The registry branch of KTB and the legal-affiliation branch of WLY permit a social-administrative model: taking Satan as patron enrolls a person in his cohort, and the imposed statement is the cohort's governing outcome. HDY then carries the enrolled member along that cohort's course.

activation_trace.role: Entry of a name into a register supplies enrollment in a class governed by the statement.
Legal and kin-like affiliation supplies the social bond defining the cohort.
A settled course supplies the collective trajectory assigned to those enrolled.

changed_reading.before: The verse states only an individual act and its individual consequence.
changed_reading.after: The verse may also picture patronage as enrollment into a governed retinue whose registered course terminates in punishment.

context_deltas.mechanism: The nearby argumentative figure first follows a rebellious Satan, then the repeated argumentative frame lacks knowledge, guidance, and an illuminating book, and finally the human figure acts to divert others from God's path. The focus relation thus propagates: Satan's follower can become the next misleader in a social relay.

activation_trace.role: Successive attachment in the focus supplies the relay structure that context develops.
Loyal following and succession make the human a downstream adherent.
The rebellious Satan identifies the upstream source being followed.
Negated true guidance marks the missing corrective route in the downstream human.
The absent written book removes a stable textual check on the relay.
The same causative diversion now belongs to the human actor, showing transmission of function.
An extended traversable path supplies what the downstream actor diverts others away from.

structural_cues: 22:3 and 22:8 repeat the argumentative-human frame; the first adds following, while 22:9 assigns that human a purpose of misleading.
The sequence moves from following a Satan to lacking guidance and book to diverting other people from a path.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated frame, followership, missing correctives, and later human misguidance; I infer a causal relay in which a follower reproduces the patron's function. A live alternative is that the repeated frames describe separate human types rather than successive stages.

changed_reading.before: Satan directly misguides one attached individual.
changed_reading.after: Satanic patronage is transmissible: the attached person can inherit the misguiding role and extend the route to further people.

context_deltas.mechanism: The harmful object of invocation is described as nearer in damage than benefit and then as both a bad patron and a bad intimate associate. This sharpens WLY in the focus from abstract assent into dangerous proximity: the patron's harm works because the person has admitted him into the near social position that conducts affairs.

activation_trace.role: Nearness without a gap anchors the focus relation as operative proximity.
Damage as the opposite of benefit supplies the relation's net output.
Nearness makes harmful access, rather than remote influence, the mechanism.
The patron who undertakes affairs identifies the harmful relation as governance.
Intermingling and association supply the social intimacy through which patronage operates.

structural_cues: 22:13 places nearer harm, bad patron, and bad associate in one compact predication.
The focus's WLY relation and 22:13's patron noun share the same root inventory.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies harm, comparative nearness, patronage, and association; I infer that proximity enables the patron's directional control. The alternative is that nearness evaluates the harm temporally or probabilistically without describing the mechanics of influence.

changed_reading.before: Taking Satan means holding a wrong belief about him.
changed_reading.after: Taking Satan means granting a harmful patron intimate access and governance, so misdirection emerges from admitted proximity.

context_deltas.mechanism: Every attempted exit from fiery anguish is answered by forced return, while the next positive scene repeats HDY toward good speech and a praised path. These opposed itineraries make guidance a destination-sensitive routing function. In the focus, Satan does not merely confuse; he delivers to and effectively seals the follower within the punitive terminus.

activation_trace.role: Direction and destination anchor the focus as an itinerary.
Return after attempted departure closes the punitive route into a loop.
Painful punishment identifies what the loop retains its occupants within.
Flame makes the retained destination materially continuous with the focus blaze.
Repeated beneficial guidance supplies a controlled contrast with the focus's hostile conductor.
The straight road makes explicit the positive itinerary against which the focus route is inverted.

structural_cues: 22:22 uses a repeated whenever-return pattern, so attempted egress never changes the destination.
22:24 immediately repeats passive HDY twice with explicit positive objects and destination.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies forced return and parallel guidance-to constructions; I infer that destination, rather than the bare routing function, determines the moral value of HDY. A live alternative keeps the focus HDY as pure verbal irony and treats the later parallel as contrast only.

changed_reading.before: The focus uses guidance sarcastically for misleading.
changed_reading.after: The hostile guidance is structurally real conveyance: it runs an opposed itinerary whose terminal system both receives and returns the follower.

context_deltas.mechanism: The falling simile supplies a physical sequence for the focus verb pair: loss begins as dislodgement, then a seizing or wind-like vector takes over and carries the person toward remoteness. Misguidance and guidance become successive phases of one trajectory, with the second phase giving direction to the first phase's instability.

activation_trace.role: Loss from the prior holder anchors the initial dislodgement in the focus.
Direction and bearing anchor the subsequent transport in the focus.
A low place that draws the faller supplies a destination-seeking dislodgement.
Swift seizure supplies the first possible external handoff after the fall.
Falling into an abyss gives the loss phase kinetic shape.
Wind as force supplies the alternate vector that takes control of the trajectory.
Distance and removal supply the vector's terminal displacement.

structural_cues: 22:31 presents a branching but continuous motion sequence: fall, then either seizure or wind-driven transport, then a remote location.
The focus likewise coordinates loss and direction under one agent and one object.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a simile of dislodgement followed by external vectors; I map that sequence onto the focus's DLL-to-HDY order and assign Satan the functional role of the vector. The alternative is that 22:31 depicts only the outcome of association and says nothing about Satan's agency.

changed_reading.before: Misguidance is a wrong proposition taught by a bad guide.
changed_reading.after: Misguidance can be a trajectory: first remove stability, then seize the resulting motion and carry the displaced person toward a remote destructive end.

context_deltas.mechanism: Satan casts material into a recited transmission; removal followed by replacement and firming exposes the insertion, while the result becomes a test for susceptible hearts before true guidance to a straight path is restated. This revises the focus from an openly rival lesson into possible channel capture: the misleader inserts a directional contaminant into material already moving through a guidance channel.

activation_trace.role: Diversion from right aim anchors the contaminant's effect in the focus.
Recitation read and placed supplies the host transmission into which material is inserted.
Throwing something down supplies the intrusive act.
The rebellious Satan identifies the contaminating actor.
Removal followed by a replacement supplies active correction of the inserted material.
Firming and exactness supply stabilization of the corrected signal.
Turning away from truth supplies the directional effect on susceptible recipients.
True gentle direction restores the uncorrupted routing function.
The straight road supplies the corrected channel's explicit destination.

structural_cues: 22:52 orders the actions as recitation, Satanic casting, divine removal, and firming of signs.
22:53-54 split the reception between tested susceptible hearts and informed believing hearts guided to a straight path.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies insertion, correction, stabilization, divergent reception, and restored guidance; I infer that the focus Satan can misguide by hijacking a guidance-bearing channel rather than only by announcing a separate route. The alternative is that 22:52-54 concerns protected prophetic transmission and should remain only an analogy to 22:4.

changed_reading.before: Satan guides by presenting a visibly separate false path.
changed_reading.after: Satan may guide toward punishment by inserting a contaminating direction into a transmission the recipient already treats as guidance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The late assertion joins exhaustive divine knowledge of heaven and earth to presence in a book and ease for God. It therefore sharpens the focus's passive decree as a registered invariant within comprehensive knowledge, not merely a prediction improvised after an individual chooses allegiance.

activation_trace.role: The imposed decree anchors the focus consequence as fixed judgment.
Disclosure to the knower supplies the comprehensive epistemic frame for the record.
A written book supplies the record in which the invariant is held.
Ease after difficulty removes any suggestion that maintaining the comprehensive record strains its author.

structural_cues: 22:70 moves from repeated divine knowing to inclusion in a book and then to ease for God.
Both 22:4 and 22:70 use KTB language with an upon construction.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies comprehensive knowledge, a written record, and divine ease; I infer that 22:4 states a durable registered rule within that record. The alternative is that the two KTB occurrences have independent local functions and should not be made one documentary mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The opening passive simply reports a sentence previously pronounced about Satan.
changed_reading.after: The opening passive evokes a durable entry in an all-encompassing record: patronage reliably instantiates an already registered relational rule.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah closes by commanding a protective hold on God, naming God the community's patron, and pairing that patronage with help. This supplies a full counter-system to the focus: attachment is unavoidable as a routing architecture, but its object determines whether the bond preserves and assists or misleads and delivers to fire.

activation_trace.role: Allegiance anchors the destructive patronage pole in the focus.
A hold that prevents and preserves supplies the counter-attachment's protective mechanics.
The patron who undertakes affairs supplies the constructive counterpart to Satanic governance.
Aid and vindication identify the positive patron's output.

structural_cues: The final ayah places holding fast, divine patronage, and help in one closing sequence.
The same WLY inventory names the focus's destructive attachment and the closing ayah's praised patron.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two WLY poles and gives the closing pole an explicit preserving hold and helping output; I infer a competing-patronage architecture spanning the surah. The alternative is that the shared root marks analogy without requiring a binary system.

changed_reading.before: The focus warns against one isolated forbidden allegiance.
changed_reading.after: The focus is one pole of a surah-wide attachment architecture: the chosen patron governs the route, with Satanic attachment displacing and burning while divine attachment holds and helps.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the surface form and destination syntax strongly favor ordinary HDY, yet the packet explicitly supplies an H-D-D mapped target for the same focus occurrence. It remains anchored as a split-root echo that adds breaking and threat to the directional verb; downstream prose should present it only as a secondary overtone, never as the primary morphological parse.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus HDY occurrence is packet-mapped both to the dominant guidance inventory and to a distinct H-D-D inventory.

activation_trace.role: Severe breaking and demolition add a destructive underside to the act of conducting.
Threat and intimidation make the hostile destination audible within the guiding verb.
Punitive pain keeps the destructive echo attached to the focus's explicit endpoint.

changed_reading.before: The second verb only means directed conveyance toward punishment.
changed_reading.after: As a contained split-root echo, the conveyance also sounds like breaking and threatening the follower into the punitive destination.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the sale-transfer branch of WLY and market-price branch of SAR are distant from the ordinary focus senses. It remains anchored in those two focus roots and is activated by the surah's explicit commercial-loss branch; downstream prose should label it a cross-domain economic metaphor, not a lexical translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus joins a WLY transaction-capable branch to a SAR destination whose inventory includes market price.

activation_trace.role: Transfer of a sale supplies the metaphor of handing oneself into another party's account.
Market price recasts the blazing endpoint as the ruinous cost posted for that transfer.
Commercial loss supplies a nearby context in which failed allegiance is evaluated as a losing transaction.

changed_reading.before: Patronage causes punishment in a purely moral sequence.
changed_reading.after: As a contained economic metaphor, patronage transfers the person into a losing account whose disclosed price is the blaze.

strongest_changes: The focus relation becomes a transmissible relay in which a follower can reproduce Satan's misguiding function.
The DLL/HDY pair becomes destination-sensitive routing, concretized by forced return to fire and contrasted with guidance to good speech and a straight path.
The final command to hold fast to the praised patron turns the focus into one pole of a competing-attachment architecture.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context turned the local verbal paradox into several inspectable mechanisms: social relay, harmful proximity, closed-loop routing, ballistic handoff, signal contamination, and a registered relational invariant.
remaining_uncertainties: The repeated argumentative-human frames may be stages in one relay or separate examples.
The insertion and correction sequence in 22:52-54 may illuminate Satanic method only analogically rather than directly.
The split-root destructive echo and commercial-price model remain branch-distant overlays, not primary parses.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Chosen adjacency becomes a binding trajectory.** `ك ت ب B003` supplies binding decree, `و ل ي B001/B004` nearness and loyal alliance, `ض ل ل B001` departure from guidance, and `ه د ي B001/B002` direction toward a way. The conditional sequence runs alliance → misdirection → guidance to punishment. I supply the causal arrow that sustained allegiance grants the followed power to set one's course. The paradoxical *yahdīhi* therefore reads as real directional guidance whose destination is ruin, not as salvific guidance.
2. **The decree joins acts to consequences.** Behind writing, `ك ت ب B001` gives joining one thing to another. The passive *kutiba* precedes tightly linked conditional clauses. I infer that what is “written” is the stable attachment of patronage to outcome. The verse can thus be read as describing an inscribed causal bond rather than an arbitrary sentence detached from the follower's choice.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 22:67-69 sharpened the distinction between directional guidance and disputation: ritual difference is not to become mutual pulling, and final separation belongs to divine judgment.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Patronage writes its own destination.** Fixed `كُتِبَ` uses `ك ت ب:B003` (inscribing as binding decree), and `تَوَلَّاه` can activate `و ل ي:B003` (assuming charge) and `B004` (loyal alliance). The syntax itself supplies the chain: whoever grants charge to the defiant guide is misled. I supply only the arrow that a governing allegiance shapes subsequent movement. The decree reads less like an unrelated sentence imposed from outside and more like the binding consequence of selected patronage.
2. **A malign use of guidance.** Fixed `يَهْدِيه` retains `ه د ي:B001` (gentle guidance toward a way), but its stated endpoint is `ع ذ ب:B005` through `س ع ر:B001` (fire kindling and blazing). `22:8-9` contrast absent guidance with diversion from God's way. The packet supplies guidance-language and the destructive destination; I infer an escort function stripped of beneficence. “Guides him” becomes grimly directional: guidance as reliable conveyance need not imply a good end.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later `22:8-9` clarified the surprise in `يَهْدِيه`: absent true guidance and diversion from a traversed way confirm that the fixed verb retains directional reliability while its endpoint becomes malign.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, anlam çekirdeğini bir şeyi başka bir şeye katıp birleştirmek olarak açıkça kurar; deri dikme, hayvanın bazı uzuvlarını bağlama, boncukla tutturma ve birlik oluşturma kullanımları da bu çekirdeğin özelleşmiş gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, yazı yazma ya da hüküm verme anlamını değil, fiziksel veya toplu birleştirme işlemini kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım ortak birleştirme çekirdeğini korur; dikme, bağlama, kapatma ve birlik düzenleme anlamlarını yalnızca tanıklanmış biçim ve yapılara bağlı özelleşmeler olarak verir.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi başka bir şeye katıp aralarında fiziksel ya da topluluk oluşturan bir bağ kurmaktır. Derileri dikme, açıklıkları bağlama veya kapatma ve insan ya da atları düzenli bir birlik hâline getirme bunun yapıya bağlı gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Temel işlem, bir şeyi başka bir şeye katarak ikisini bir bütün veya bağlı bir düzen içinde birleştirmektir.
Deri parçalarını ya da bir su tulumunu dikişle birleştirmek, çekirdeğin el işi alanındaki özel gerçekleşmesidir.
Bir hayvanın belirli uzuvlarını halka, kayış veya iple birbirine bağlamak ve bir kabın ağzını sıkıca kapatmak yapıya bağlı kullanımlardır.
Atların veya askerlerin toplanıp ayrı ve düzenli bir birlik oluşturması, fiziksel birleştirmeden topluluk düzenine uzanan anlamdır.
Kayışın iki yüzünü bir arada tutan boncuk, ortaya çıkan bağın somut bir örneğidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, katma ve birleştirme çekirdeğinin dikiş, bağlama, sıkıca kapatma ve düzenli topluluk oluşturma gibi somut uygulamalarda korunmasıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi harfleri çizgiyle düzenleyerek yazma işlemini, bunun ürünü olan yazılı metin veya sayfayı ve yazdırma, isteme ya da öğretme gibi yapıya bağlı kullanımları birlikte tanıklar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, yazı üretimi ve yazılı ürünle sınırlıdır; yazının bağlayıcı hüküm için mecazlaşması ayrı dalda tutulur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yazma işlemi ve yazılı ürün dalın merkezindedir; dikte ettirme, başkasından yazmasını isteme ve yazmayı öğretme anlamları yalnızca ilgili yapılara bağlı olarak korunur.

concept_map.definition: Harfleri çizgiyle düzenleyerek yazılı bir metin oluşturmak ve bu işlemin ürünü olan metin ya da yazılı sayfadır. Birine yazdırma, ondan yazmasını isteme ve yazmayı öğretme ise belirli yapılara bağlı uzantılardır.

facets.statement: Temel işlem, harfleri yazıyla düzenleyip bir metin oluşturmak veya var olan metni kopyalamaktır.
İşlemin ürünü, yazılmış metin veya üzerinde bu metnin bulunduğu sayfa ya da kitaptır.
Bir metni başkasına söyleyerek yazdırmak ve birinden kendisi için yazmasını istemek yapıya bağlı ettirgen ve isteme kullanımlarıdır.
Yazmayı öğretmek, yazı öğretmeni ve öğretim yeri anlamları yazı edinimi alanındaki bağlı kullanımlardır.
Öğretim yerindeki çocuklar veya onların topluluğu için kullanılan biçim, yeri değil öğrencileri gösterir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar yazmayı harfleri çizgiyle bir araya getiren işlem olarak sunar; yazılı ürün, kopyalama, dikte ettirme, yazma isteği ve öğretimle ilgili kullanımlar bu merkeze bağlanır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi yükümlülük, hüküm, paylaştırılmış yazgı veya kesinleşmiş karar olarak belirleme alanını açıkça toplar; burada yazı, harf çizme eylemi değil bağlayıcı biçimde belirlemenin anlatım yoludur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Salt yazı yazmak bu dala girmez; belirleme işleminin yükümlülük, hüküm veya yazgı sonucu doğurması gerekir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yükümlülük, hüküm ve yazgı değerleri birlikte korunur; birine zorunluluk yükleme ve Tanrı'nın belirlemesi anlamları yalnızca tanıklanmış yapılara bağlanır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi bağlayıcı bir yükümlülük, hüküm veya gerçekleşmesi belirlenmiş pay ve yazgı olarak karara bağlamaktır. Yazma çağrışımı burada harf çizmekten çok kararın kesinleştirilip geçerli kılınmasını anlatır.

facets.statement: Bir işi yapılması gereken bağlayıcı bir yükümlülük olarak belirlemek temel değerlerden biridir.
Bir konuda geçerli ve kesinleşmiş hüküm vermek aynı belirleme çekirdeğinin yargısal yönüdür.
Bir olayın payını, ölçüsünü veya gelecekte gerçekleşecek sonucunu önceden belirlemek yazgı yönünü oluşturur.
Yazma anlatımı, belirlenen hükmün saptanmış, yürürlüğe konmuş ve kesinleşmiş olmasını ifade eder.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar yükümlülük, hüküm, yazgı, belirleme ve kesinleşmiş karar değerlerini aynı bağlayıcı saptama alanında birleştirir; yazma sözü bu saptamanın anlatım aracıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir kişinin adını pay veya geçim kaydına ya da yönetim siciline geçirmek ile kişiyi tanıklar topluluğuna dâhil etmek arasında ortak bir kayıt ve üyelik çekirdeği kurar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, genel yazma eylemini değil, adı kayda geçirerek kişiyi bir listeye veya belirli topluluğa dâhil etmeyi anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Sicile alma ve topluluğa katma çekirdeği korunur; pay kaydı, yönetim sicili ve tanıklar arasına katılma anlamları kendi tanıklanmış yapılarıyla sınırlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin adını resmî bir pay, geçim veya yönetim kaydına geçirerek onu kayıtlılar arasına almak ya da kişiyi belirli bir topluluğun üyesi saymaktır.

facets.statement: Kişinin adını bir kayıt veya listeye geçirerek ona kayıtlı kişi konumu vermek dalın çekirdeğidir.
Adı pay, geçim tahsisatı veya yönetim siciline yazdırmak resmî kayıt alanındaki özel gerçekleşmedir.
Bir kişiyi tanıklar gibi belirli bir topluluğun içinde saymak, sicile almadan üyelik vermeye uzanan kullanımdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak içeriği, adı kayda geçirmenin kişiyi pay alanlar, yönetim sicilindekiler veya belirli bir topluluğun üyeleri arasına sokmasıdır.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, her türlü yazılı sözleşmeyi değil, bedelin ödenmesiyle özgürlüğe götüren bu özel sözleşme türünü kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım özel sözleşme türüne bağlı kalır; sözleşmenin adı, tarafı ve sözleşme yapma eylemi ayrı tanıklanmış biçimler olarak korunur ve genel sözleşme anlamına genişletilmez.

facets.statement: Sahip ile köleleştirilmiş kişi arasında, kişinin kendi özgürlük bedelini ödemesini konu alan özel bir sözleşme kurulur.
Bedel belirlenmiş ödeme dilimlerine bağlanır ve köleleştirilmiş kişi bunu kendi kazancından karşılar.
Kararlaştırılan bedelin tamamlanması sözleşmenin sonucu olarak köleleştirilmiş kişinin özgür olmasını sağlar.
İlgili biçimler sözleşmenin kendisini, sözleşmeye bağlı köleleştirilmiş kişiyi ve bağlama göre sözleşmenin öteki tarafını gösterebilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, hareketli bir şeyin sahibinden gitmesini ve sabit bir yerin konumuna ulaşamamayı aynı bulamama alanında toplar. Kanın öçsüz kalması ise kaybın sahiplik değil karşılık ve talep bakımından kurulduğu özel, kalıba bağlı bir uzantıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin sahibinin elinden çıkması veya kişinin hareketli bir şeyi ya da sabit bir yerin konumunu bulamamasıdır. Özel bir kullanımda öldürülen kişinin kanı öç alınmadan ve karşılık aranmadan kalır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyin sahibinden gitmesi ve nerede olduğunun bilinememesi temel yitirme ilişkisidir.
Ev, ibadet yeri veya başka sabit bir yerin konumuna ulaşamamak, nesneyi değil yolu bulamama biçimidir.
